ca_wedge_the_2.blurb: The Wedge is a pinnacle on the Jumbo Rock side of Joshua Tree National Park, set just off the paved road where it forms the end of Cunning Rock. It has nine routes spread across trad, bolted sport and top-rope, running from about 5.6 up to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common grade. The surface is very coarse, which gives plenty of friction, and the wall is shielded from wind, so it feels comfortable on sunny days. The walk in from the roadside pullout takes roughly ten to fifteen minutes through a gap in the first formations.

ca_whitney_portal_buttress.blurb: Whitney Portal Buttress is the big cliff rising to the north above the Whitney Portal parking lot, near Lone Pine on the Eastern Sierra side, at roughly 9,000 feet. The climbing is all trad, mostly long multi-pitch lines, with several running to eight pitches and a few shorter ones. Grades are concentrated around 5.10, with a couple of lines up near 5.12. To reach the base, follow the Mount Whitney Trail until it bends west, then head straight up to the rock.

ca_upper_crust_2.blurb: Upper Crust is a sport crag in the Central Gorge stretch of Owens River Gorge near Bishop, at about 5,300 feet. It sits up and to the left of the Social Platform when viewed from the river, and it was once part of that wall. There are nine routes, mostly bolted with two trad lines, ranging from 5.8 up to 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. The left half picks up afternoon sun, while the right half stays shaded from morning into early afternoon, so you can choose a side to suit the temperature.

ca_roadside_fire_boulder.blurb: Roadside Fire Boulder is a single boulder beside the road in the South Lake area of the Bishop region, on the Eastern Sierra side. It has nine problems, from V0 up to V7, with the largest share in the V0 to V2 range and a handful of harder lines above that. The setting is a short stroll from a dirt pullout along a trail, so it fits a quick session with pads, or an add-on stop while visiting the other South Lake climbing nearby.

ca_under_taker_crag.blurb: Under Taker Crag is a large, prominent mass of rock in the Horsemen's Center part of the Apple Valley area, in California's High Desert at about 3,200 feet. It stands east of the parking area, above a water tank. There are nine climbs: six sport routes, one trad line, one top-rope and one boulder problem, from 5.6 to 5.12 with a small cluster in 5.11. It belongs to the BMX Crags, a spread of walls that collect lots of sun, which makes it a warm choice through the winter, and the base offers wide views over the surrounding desert.
